questions.question: The presiding officer of the Lok Sabha is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Speaker**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Speaker ** ​

 
 
• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is the presiding officer of the Lok Sabha.
 
• The speaker is elected generally in the first meeting of the Lok Sabha following general elections.
 
• The speaker of Lok Sabha is elected by all Members of the Lok Sabha.
 
• First meeting of the Lok Sabha is presided over by Pro Tem Speaker.
 
• He will be presiding officer of Lok Sabha till the time, the elected speaker of Lok Sabha takes his seat.
 
• Lok sabha speaker has the power to choose whether bill is a money bill or not. His decision is final and cannot be questioned in court.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lok Sabha**

 
 
• Lok Sabha is the lower house of India's bicameral Parliament.
 
• The Hindi name of Lok Sabha was adopted by the house of the people on 14th May 1954.
 
• The full term of a Lok Sabha is 5 years.
 
• Fifth Lok Sabha from 1971 to 1977(5 years 10 months and 6 days) is the longest Lok Sabha in India.
 
• Twelfth Lok Sabha from 1998 to 1999(1 year 1 month and 4 days) is the shortest Lok Sabha in India.
 
• Lok Sabha is constituted under article 81 of the constitution.
 
• G. V Mavlankar is the father of Lok Sabha.
 
• The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is fixed at 552.
 
• Money bill can introduce only in Lok Sabha and not in Rajya Sabha.
 
• A resolution to discontinue a national emergency can be passed on by the Lok Sabha.
 
• Uttar Pradesh has the maximum membership in Lok Sabha.

questions.question: Which among the following is the coldest of the atmospheric layers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mesosphere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **M**esosphere

 
 
• It lies above the stratosphere, which extends up to a height of 80 km.
 
• In this layer, once again, the temperature starts decreasing with the increase in altitude and reaches up to minus 100°C at a height of 80 km.
 
• The upper limit of the mesosphere is known as mesopause​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **S**tratosphere

 
 
• It is found above the tropopause and extends up to a height of 50 km.
 
• One important feature of the stratosphere is that it contains the ozone layer.
 
• This layer absorbs ultra-violet radiation and shields life on the earth from an intense, harmful form of energy.
 
• The stratopause caps the top of the stratosphere.
 
 
 
• **Thermosphere ****​**
 
 
• It is located between 80 and 400 km above the mesopause.
 
• It contains electrically charged particles known as ions, and hence, it is also known as the ionosphere.
 
• Radio waves transmitted from the earth are reflected back to the earth by this layer.
 
• The temperature here starts increasing with height.
 
 
 
• **Troposphere**
 
 
• Its average height is 13 km.
 
• Troposphere is the densest layer of all.
 
• The air we breathe exists here.
 
• Almost all the weather phenomena like rainfall, fog, and hailstorm occur in this layer.

questions.question: Who among the following wrote the biography of Jahangir known as Iqbalnama-i Jahangiri?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is - Mutamid Khan**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mutamid Khan**

 
 
• Mutamid Khan authored the biography of Jahangir known as "Iqbalnama-i Jahangiri".
 
• The work provides detailed accounts and chronicles of the reign of Emperor Jahangir, including significant events of his rule.
 
• It is an essential primary source for historians studying the Mughal period, offering insights into Jahangir's administration, personal life, and the socio-political scenario of the time.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inayat Khan**

 
 
• Inayat Khan was a noble in the court of Shah Jahan and wrote "Shah Jahan Nama," which chronicles the reign of Emperor Shah Jahan.
 
• His work provides insights into Shah Jahan's rule, including his architectural achievements and administrative measures.
 
 
 
• **Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan**
 
 
• Abdul Rahim was one of the Navaratnas (Nine Gems) in the court of Emperor Akbar and was known for his poetry, translation work, and patronage of arts.
 
• Though notable for his contributions, he did not write about Jahangir but was involved in translating "Baburnama" into Persian.
 
 
 
• **Abul Fazl**
 
 
• Abul Fazl was a close advisor of Emperor Akbar and one of the Navaratnas in his court.
 
• He authored the "Akbarnama," a three-volume history of Akbar's reign, and the "Ain-i-Akbari", which details the administrative system of the Mughal Empire.
 
• His comprehensive works are critical for understanding Akbar's imperial policies and governance.

questions.question: ______ was founded by Dadoba Pandurang and his brother Atmaram Pandurang in 1867.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prarthana Samaj**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dadoba** Pandurang and his brother** Atmaram Pandurang** founded the **Prarthana Samaj** in **1867**.
 
• **This socio-religious reform movement** emerged in** Bombay (now Mumbai), India**, aiming to make religious and social changes to Hindu society.
 
• It was significantly influenced by the** Brahmo Samaj **and shared many similarities with this **reformist movement.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tattvabodhini Sabha: **

 
 
• This was a **Hindu reformist group** founded in Calcutta, India, in 1839 by Debendranath Tagore.
 
• It played a significant role in initially propagating Brahmoism, which eventually evolved into the Brahmo Samaj.
 
 
 
• **Brahmo Samaj: **
 
 
• Founded in** 1828** by** Raja Ram Mohan Roy.**
 
• The Brahmo Samaj is a **social-religious reform movement**
 
• It promoted monotheism and opposed practices such as idol worship and sati.
 
 
 
• **Arya Samaj:**
 
 
• Founded by **Swami Dayananda Saraswati** in **1875.**
 
• Arya Samaj is a Hindu reform movement that rejects i**dol worship, casteism, and rituals**, placing its faith in the teachings of the ancient **Vedas.**
 
• It advocates for the infallible authority of the **Vedas** and promotes concepts such as karma and reincarnation.

questions.question: What is the major function of a cell wall?

options.text: It works as a storage for material
It provides shape and rigidity to the cell
It is responsible for cell division
It helps in synthesis of carbohydrate

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It provides shape and rigidity to the cell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cell walls **are a feature of almost all** prokaryotic cells**, as well as many **eukaryotic organisms.**
 
• In addition to providing structural support and maintaining the shape of the cell, The cell wall serves as a **protective barrier** against **physical** and** biological threats.**
 
• It also allows the cell to **withstand** the difference in **osmotic pressure** between the **cell's interior and its environment.**
 
• However, it is not primarily involved in functions such as storage of material, cell division, or the synthesis of carbohydrates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** The structure of a typical cell, whether it is a **prokaryotic cell (such as bacteria)** or a **eukaryotic cell (like those found in plants and animals),** includes several key components:

 
• **Cell Membrane (Plasma Membrane):** It controls the movement of substances in and out of the cell.
 
• **Cytoplasm: **This is the jelly-like substance within the cell membrane, which contains all the organelles.
 
• **Nucleus:** In eukaryotic cells, this organelle contains the cell's DNA and controls the cell's growth, metabolism, and reproduction.
 
• **Mitochondria: ** They generate most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER):** There are two types: rough ER, which has ribosomes on its surface, and smooth ER, which lacks ribosomes.
 
• **Golgi Apparatus:** This organelle is involved in the modification, sorting, and packaging of proteins for secretion.
 
• **Lysosomes: **They digest excess or worn-out organelles, food particles, and engulfed viruses or bacteria.
 
• **Ribosomes:** They can be found either floating freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum.
 
• **Vacuoles:** These are storage bubbles found in cells. 
 
• **Cell Wall (only in plant cells, fungi, and some protists and bacteria):** It provides and maintains the shape of these cells and serves as a protective barrier.
 
• **Chloroplasts (only in plant cells and some protists):** They are the site of photosynthesis, where light energy is converted into chemical energy.

questions.question: Which article of the constitution of India lays down the uniform civil code?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 44**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 44** is part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy.**
 
• It urges the** state to strive for a Uniform Civil Code for all citizens, regardless of their religion.**
 
• This would mean a common set of laws governing personal matters like **marriage, divorce, inheritance, etc., for all citizens.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 377: **
 
• **This article** does not exist in** the Indian Constitution.**
 
• However, **Section 377** of the Indian Penal Code was a colonial-era law that criminalized homosexual acts, which was decriminalized by the **Supreme Court of India in 2018.**
 
• **Article 370: **
 
• This article gave special autonomous status to the state of **Jammu and Kashmir,** allowing it to have its constitution,** flag, and autonomy** over internal administration.
 
• However, in August 2019, the Indian government abrogated most provisions of **Article 370.**
 
• **Article 12: **
 
• This article is part of the** Fundamental Rights in Part III of the Indian Constitution.**
 
• It provides the definition of the **State **and the authorities against whom **Fundamental Rights** can be enforced.

questions.question: Which among the following instruments is used for measuring the humidity of the air or a gas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hygrometer**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Hygrometer:

 
 
• This is a device used to measure the amount of humidity and water vapor in the atmosphere, in soil, or in confined spaces.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This is an instrument used to **measure the power of incident electromagnetic radiation.**

• Hydrometer:
 
 
• This is an instrument used to measure the specific gravity (or relative density) of liquids
 
• That is the ratio of the density of the liquid to the density of water.
 
 
 
• **Altimeter:**
 
 
• This is an instrument used to **measure the altitude of an object above a fixed level.**
 
• The true altitude is the elevation above mean sea level.
 
• Altimeters are commonly used in **aircraft, hiking, and mountain climbing.**

questions.question: ______ is used for the separation of components of a mixture containing two miscible liquids that boil without decomposition and have sufficient difference in their boiling points.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Distillation**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Distillation**:
 
• This is a process used to **separate components of a mixture using differences in their boiling points.**
 
• The mixture is heated to a temperature at which** one or more components evaporate, and then the vapor is condensed and collected separately.**
 
• It's commonly used to **purify liquids, such as alcohol or water, or to separate petroleum into various components, from gasoline to tar.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbonation:**

 
 
• This is the process of dissolving carbon dioxide in water.
 
• The process usually involves pressure and low temperatures.
 
• When the pressure is reduced, the carbon dioxide is released from the solution as small bubbles,
 
• Which gives the solution a fizzy taste. It is commonly used in the creation of soft drinks.
 
 
 
• **Sublimation:**
 
 
• This is a process in which a substance goes directly from the solid phase to the gas phase, skipping the liquid phase.
 
• Dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) is a common example of a substance that sublimates.
 
• This process can be used to purify certain substances that sublimate, such as iodine or naphthalene (mothballs).
 
 
 
• **Emulsification: **
 
 
• This is the process of mixing two or more immiscible (unblendable) substances.
 
• This is typically accomplished with the help of a third substance called an emulsifier or emulsifying agent
 
• Which is soluble in both of the mixed substances.
 
• Mayonnaise is a common example of an emulsion
 
• Where oil and vinegar (which are normally immiscible) are mixed together using egg yolk as an emulsifier.

questions.question: Late Jagjit Singh was a popular composer and a ______ singer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghazal**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ghazal Singer:**
 
• A Ghazal singer performs the Ghazal, a form of amatory poem or ode, originating in Arabic poetry.
 
• Ghazals are traditionally expressions of love, loss, and longing. 
 
• Late Jagjit Singh was a popular composer and a Ghazal Singer

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Opera Singer:**
 
• An opera singer performs in a kind of performance in which music has a leading role and the parts are taken by singers.
 
• Opera incorporates many of the elements of spoken theatre, such as acting, scenery, and costumes and sometimes includes dance.
 
• **Rock Singer:**
 
• A rock singer sings rock music, a genre that originated as "rock and roll" in the United States in the 1950s, and developed into a range of different styles in the 1960s and later
 
• The sound of rock often revolves around the electric guitar or acoustic guitar, and it uses a strong back beat laid down by a rhythm section.
 
• **Pop Singer: **
 
• A pop singer performs pop music, a genre of popular music that originated in its modern form during the mid-1950s in the United States and the United Kingdom.
 
• The terms "popular music" and "pop music" are often used interchangeably, although the former describes all music that is popular and includes many disparate styles.

questions.question: The number of times a unit of money changes hands during the unit period is called the _______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**velocity of circulation of money**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The velocity of money **refers to how often one unit of currency is used for purchases in a given time period.**
 
• It's calculated by dividing the** nominal GDP by the total amount of money supply.**
 
• High velocity indicates a **healthy economy and low velocity can indicate a sluggish economy.**
 
• Understanding the velocity of money assists central banks in formulating monetary policy.
 
• **High velocity can sometimes be associated with inflation, though the relationship is complex.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Base Money: **Also known as high-powered money, **it consists of physical currency (coins and paper money) and central bank reserves**, representing the base upon which the larger commercial banking system can create additional money through loans.
 
• **Remittances:** These are funds transferred by **migrant workers back to their home country, playing a crucial role in the economies of many developing countries.**
 
• **Zero Economic Profit: **It occurs when a** firm's total revenues are exactly equal to its total opportunity costs, including both explicit and implicit costs, meaning the firm is just covering all its costs but not making any surplus profits.**

questions.question: Who among the following won the Meltwater Champions Chess Tour 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnus Carlsen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Magnus Carlsen **secured the **overall Meltwater Champions Chess Tour title for the second consecutive year, confirming his win even with one event left.**
 
• He earned a **$50,000 prize from the Aimchess Rapid semi-finals, **increasing his total tour winnings to **$192,500 and earning the title of 2022 Tour Champion.**
 
• **Norwegian Magnus Carlsen is currently the world number 1 in chess and is pursuing a third consecutive tournament victory in the tour's penultimate event.**
 
• Polish player Jan-Krzysztof Duda was the only competitor who could have challenged Carlsen's lead but required Indian teen Arjun Erigaisi to eliminate Carlsen and win the final Major of the season.
 
• In the quarter-finals, Carlsen faced significant competition from Erigaisi, who initially led the game with three pawns more than Carlsen.
 
• **Despite Erigaisi's early lead, Carlsen used his endgame skills to recover, eventually forcing a draw after a marathon 137 moves.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• The tour includes several types of events, such as regular tournaments,** "majors", and a final tournament, with different point values assigned to each for determining the overall tour standings.**
 
• Each event in the tour is hosted on the chess platform **chess24, and games are live-streamed with commentary for viewers to watch in real-time.**
 
• **With substantial cash prizes and a high level of competition, the Meltwater Champions Chess Tour is considered one of the premier events in online chess.**

questions.question: Who among the following Mughal emperors built Sheesh Mahal in Agra?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shah Jahan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shah Jahan**, whose name means** "King of the World" in Persian, was the fifth Mughal emperor, who ruled from 1628 to 1658.**
 
• Known for his patronage of the arts, **Shah Jahan commissioned many magnificent architectural projects during his reign, with the Sheesh Mahal in Agra being one of them.**
 
• Sheesh Mahal, also known as **"Glass Palace", is situated inside the Agra Fort. It's renowned for its intricate mirror work.**
 
• Shah Jahan is most famous for the construction of the** Taj Mahal, built in memory of his beloved wife, Mumtaz Mahal.**
 
• His architectural** style often involved white marble and precious stones, leading to some of the most beautiful and iconic structures in India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
